clue.text: Administer curare to Jean-Claude Juncker?

indicators.note: to administer is to manage or dispense, so these letters are dispensed afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A darkly comic suggestion to poison the former European Commission president with a South American arrow poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Juncker headed the European Commission, so he is an example of a Brussels official; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Most senior leaders of European lands declare emergency, summon Tsipras

indicators.note: the leaders of these six words are their opening letters, read in order

parts.words: European lands declare emergency, summon Tsipras

explanation.surface: A news headline: Europe's senior figures call a crisis summit and summon the Greek prime minister Alexis Tsipras.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest member of a family is its most senior, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Whistleblower in Europe's to get rid of undesirables

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, and REF is the short form
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A political story about an informant inside the European institutions and a purge of unwanted elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests an informant, but here it is the football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to purify it by removing impurities, the unwanted parts.

clue.text: Swiss city's aloof wartime leader

parts.note: Chur is the capital of the Swiss canton of Graubunden
chill describes a cold, distant manner

explanation.surface: A Swiss town with a standoffish commander in time of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's prime minister through most of the Second World War.

clue.text: Greek finding a source of cash here?

definitions.meaning: ... Greek is the classical dialect of Athens and its region

definitions.text: finding a source of cash here?
definitions.meaning: a loft is where forgotten heirlooms that might be sold are found

explanation.definitionFit: Attica is the region round Athens, giving its adjective; the top room of a house is where valuables get rediscovered.

clue.text: War-torn country entertains leader of Zambia's ruling party

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Syria has been ravaged by civil war

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A war-ravaged state hosts the head of an African governing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Syriza was the left-wing coalition governing Greece during the 2015 debt crisis.

clue.text: Building Chay Blyth's penultimate boat?

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are put together into a new shape
the penultimate letter of a word is the one just before its last

explanation.surface: The round-the-world yachtsman Chay Blyth constructing a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges the yachtsman's first name; 'penultimate' takes the second-last letter of his surname. Chay Blyth is a British sailor who sailed single-handed round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing or racing vessel of this kind is one type of boat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Unable to move — frozen axle, reportedly

definitions.meaning: trapped and immobile, like a ship stuck in sea ice
axle sounds like axel, a skating leap, which is a jump on the ice

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a punning description: an axel, said like 'axle', is a bound on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship trapped in pack ice cannot move; the second half plays on a figure-skating jump.

clue.text: Hera, then Ianthe, embraced troubled citizen

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the letters sit inside these names

explanation.surface: Two women from Greek myth hugging someone in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Greece's capital during the debt crisis was a citizen with troubles.

clue.text: One attacks Knut's dog "Emperor" — tail bitten off

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so 'Knut is' becomes 'I am', shortened to I'M
a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: losing a tail means the final letter of the emperor's name is dropped

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: The setter's pet dog, named Emperor, savages someone and has its tail bitten off.
explanation.walkthrough: Knut is the setter, so his 's stands for 'I is' read as I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who impugns challenges or assails another's claims, so is an attacker.

clue.text: Notes poor service — don't pay the bill

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
in tennis a fault is a bad serve

explanation.surface: A diner notes the poor service and refuses to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like restaurant service, but is the tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To default is to fail to make a payment that is owed, as Greece threatened to.

clue.text: American subject claiming honour killing unhinged his wife

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Americans call the school subject mathematics MATH
the CBE (Commander of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A news story about an American honour killing that drove a man's wife mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish king murdered Duncan, and the guilt drove Lady Macbeth mad, so his killing unhinged his wife.

clue.text: Prickly character when animated collecting coins desperately

indicators.note: acting desperately is acting wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A cartoon hedgehog frantically gathering coins, as in a video game.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog is a spiky video-game hero who also stars in cartoons.

clue.text: One of six not unknown to go from 10/1?

indicators.note: not tells us the letter standing for the unknown is left out

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Reads like a racing tip: one of six well-known runners priced at ten to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes Y from COUNTY DOWN. '10/1' looks like betting odds but is a count from ten to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting backwards from ten to one, as before a rocket launch, is counting down; the question mark marks the playful reading.

clue.text: Häagen-Dazs has this secret plan

definitions.meaning: the brand name conceals the word for a meeting's list of business within its letters

explanation.walkthrough: The ice-cream brand literally contains 'agenda' tucked in its spelling, so it has one concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: An undeclared ulterior motive is a secret scheme, an idiom; the brand name literally conceals a list of items.

clue.text: Most squat when returning mud pies thrown first

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word mud is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first of the word thrown is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Children making mud pies and throwing them when they come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' looks like an anagram signal, but only its first letter is used; 'pies' stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumpy means short and stout, so the superlative is the squattest.

clue.text: "I'm no lap-dog!" snarled Alexis Tsipras, initially enraged

indicators.note: snarled means tangled up, so these letters are knotted into a new order
initially means taking the opening letter of each name

explanation.surface: The angry Greek prime minister protests that he is nobody's poodle.
explanation.definitionFit: This huge dog breed is far too big to sit on anyone's knee, so it could say it is no lap dog.

clue.text: Accompany young woman in dancing tango

indicators.note: in places the young woman within the jumbled dance
dancing means moving about, so the letters of the dance are moved around

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl joins in an Argentine dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges TANGO into TAONG, and GAL goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to follow or go with someone, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Nits changed order for kitchen aid

indicators.note: changed order means the two words of the phrase swap places

parts.note: nits are the eggs of head lice, so the phrase is lice eggs

explanation.surface: Head lice eggs reordered to make a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nits' gives LICE EGGS; 'changed order' moves LICE behind EGGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slotted flat spatula used to lift fried eggs from the pan is a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: She excites all adult Greek men

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the words as written, with adult shortened to A, its film-rating abbreviation

explanation.surface: A woman who thrills every grown Greek man.
explanation.definitionFit: The German chancellor during the Greek crisis was a woman, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: Spot woman's instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Catch sight of a lady's musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a verb, but it is a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat stringed instrument plucked on the lap, as in Alpine folk music.

clue.text: Paint late King holding gold first edition

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the king's letters go round the rest

parts.note: the late blues guitarist B.B. King, so BB

indicators.note: first puts the edition ahead of the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A deceased monarch's painting containing a gilded first edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late King' is not a dead monarch but the blues guitarist B.B. King, who died in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear with paint crudely, so it means to paint.

clue.text: Australia? The truth: not very harsh climate

parts.note: Aust is a standard abbreviation for Australia

indicators.note: not here tells us to remove the letter that stands for very

parts.note: verity means truth

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Australia's weather is truly not so bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climate' is the economic climate: the cuts imposed on Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe economic belt-tightening creates a hard climate for a country, the political sense of severity.

clue.text: City oil scandal is something liable to infect the entire system

definitions.text: something liable to infect the entire system

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: a scandal is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A financial scandal over oil in the City threatens to contaminate the whole economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infect the entire system' sounds like financial contagion but means the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: This gut bacterium can cause food poisoning that spreads through the body.

clue.text: Person to person call ringing out in Switzerland

definitions.text: Person to person call ringing out in Switzerland

parts.words: Person to person call ringing out in Switzerland
parts.note: a person-to-person call is usually a telephone booking, but here it is a mountain singer calling to another across a valley

explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders sing this warbling call across valleys, a person calling to another.

clue.text: Some stomach hallucinogenic experience on drug

parts.note: a trip is the effect of taking a hallucinogen
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone tripping after taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle eaten as food, so part of a stomach.

clue.text: Possibly collects Roy's missing book?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for book is taken out

parts.note: the singer Roy Orbison, with the possessive giving ORBISONS

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up Roy's lost book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for short prayers in the liturgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Collects are short liturgical prayers, so they are an example of prayers in general.

clue.text: Excitement about Switzerland's currency of the future?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: drama means excitement or fuss
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A fuss over whether the Swiss franc is the money of tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece's old currency, which it might return to if it left the euro.

clue.text: Fool the king into leaving currency for 27?

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: git is British slang for a foolish person
Rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An idiot drives the monarch to abandon the money for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined term for Greece exiting the euro and returning to its old currency.

clue.text: One perhaps tastily dressed American clubber dancing

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A stylishly dressed American night-clubber on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tastily dressed' suggests fashion, but means prepared with a dressing as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed crab is a seafood dish, so this crustacean is one example served dressed.
